title: Preparing Django for Production
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of preparing django for production and at least two listed subtopics.
Interpret the preparing django for production example and predict its expected result.
Choose a verification step and identify one version, security, data, or troubleshooting consideration.

content.intro: Learn preparing django for production through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Preparing Django for Production matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines preparing django for production as part of deployment and production operations. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Development versus production settings; Dependency management; Configuration validation; Application checks; Production readiness review. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Development versus production settings
items.text: Production readiness requires environment-specific settings, secrets, allowed hosts, HTTPS, database/static/media configuration, checks, tested migration/rollback plans, logging, monitoring, and backups.

items.title: Dependency management
items.text: For Dependency management, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Configuration validation
items.text: Configuration for Configuration validation should be explicit, environment-aware, and validated before serving requests. Record defaults and deploy-specific values, keep secrets outside committed content, and test the setting that changes behavior.

items.title: Application checks
items.text: Treat Application checks as a reproducible diagnostic: capture the exact input and observed result, isolate one hypothesis, and add a regression test once the cause is fixed. Avoid exposing internal stack traces or secrets to public users.

items.title: Production readiness review
items.text: Production readiness requires environment-specific settings, secrets, allowed hosts, HTTPS, database/static/media configuration, checks, tested migration/rollback plans, logging, monitoring, and backups.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Preparing Django for Production
content_blocks.code:
python manage.py check
python manage.py check --deploy
content_blocks.expected_output: The first runs general project checks; the deployment check reports configuration issues that need review for production.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a local project using the documented Django 6.1-compatible Python environment. If this snippet depends on model names, URL configuration, settings, or an optional package, add those prerequisites before running it. Otherwise inspect it as a static example. CodeLeaf browser preview does not execute Django/Python server code.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: Run from the correct environment and with production-like settings. Warnings need triage; a clean check is not a substitute for testing or security review.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: First identify the input and the responsible Django component. Next trace how the example moves through “Preparing Django for Production” and the related concept “Development versus production settings”. Predict the result before running or inspecting it. Finally compare the observed behavior with the expected result and the cited official documentation.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Development versus production settings. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to describe preparing django for production, explain the listed topics, inspect the example, and choose an appropriate verification step. Keep the scope and version caveat visible when sharing your solution.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a framework fragment without its imports, configuration, model, or URL context.
common_mistakes.why: The snippet may be incomplete when separated from a Django project.
common_mistakes.fix: Use the stated prerequisites and run the relevant management check or focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Trusting input or relying only on a happy-path example.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid values, unauthorized requests, or concurrent activity can violate assumptions.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate on the server and add a negative or boundary test.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating the development sample as production-ready.
common_mistakes.why: Production hosting, secrets, storage, monitoring and resource limits differ from local use.
common_mistakes.fix: Follow the current deployment/security references and document untested areas.
